facts.t: The Constitution was handwritten, not typed
facts.d: Calligrapher Prem Behari Narain Raizada wrote the entire document in flowing italic script by hand. He refused payment, asking only that he be allowed to write his name on every page — and his grandfather's name on the last.

Nandalal Bose and his students decorated each Part of the Constitution with scenes from Indian history — Mohenjodaro, the Ramayana, the Buddha, Akbar, Gandhi's Dandi March. The rights of citizens open with a scene from the Gita.

Among the 389 members were 15 women, including Hansa Mehta, Sarojini Naidu, Durgabai Deshmukh, Rajkumari Amrit Kaur and Dakshayani Velayudhan — the only Dalit woman in the Assembly. Hansa Mehta is credited with changing the UDHR line from all men to all human beings.

bank.q: With reference to the composition of the Constituent Assembly, consider the following statements:
s: Members from British Indian provinces were indirectly elected by the provincial legislative assemblies.
The Assembly was elected on the basis of universal adult franchise.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is the standard trap — the body that gave India universal adult suffrage was not itself elected by it.

bank.q: Match List I (source constitution) with List II (feature borrowed):
pairs: 1. Joint sitting of the two Houses
3. Election of members to the Upper House
bank.e: Ireland → DPSP; Canada → residuary powers; Australia → joint sitting; South Africa → the manner of electing Rajya Sabha members. Germany contributed emergency provisions, the UK parliamentary government, the US Fundamental Rights.

bank.q: Which one of the following statements about the Drafting Committee is NOT correct?
o: B. N. Rau served as Constitutional Adviser and prepared the initial draft
Dr B. R. Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee
B. N. Rau was the Chairman of the Drafting Committee
The Drafting Committee scrutinised rather than originated the first draft
bank.e: B. N. Rau was Constitutional Adviser, not Chairman. Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee, which scrutinised the draft Rau had prepared — a distinction examiners exploit constantly.

bank.q: The Objectives Resolution was moved in the Constituent Assembly by:
o: Dr B. R. Ambedkar on 4 November 1948
bank.e: Nehru moved it on 13 December 1946 — four days after the first sitting. It laid down sovereignty, republicanism, democracy, justice and rights, and later shaped the Preamble.

bank.as: The Constituent Assembly was not a fully sovereign body when it first met.
bank.rs: It had been constituted under the Cabinet Mission Plan of the British government.
bank.e: Both true, and the Reason explains the Assertion. The Assembly's sovereignty came later — in spirit after Independence and in law once it also began functioning as the Dominion legislature.

bank.q: Arrange the following milestones of the Constituent Assembly in chronological order:
bank.e: First sitting 9 December 1946 → Objectives Resolution 13 December 1946 → Draft published February 1948 → Constitution enacted 26 November 1949.

bank.q: Consider the following figures relating to the Constituent Assembly:
s: It sat for 11 sessions spread over almost three years.
It met for 165 days, of which 114 were spent considering the Draft Constitution.
Ambedkar noted that 2,473 amendments were dealt with.
bank.e: All three are correct. The finer point often missed: of the 165 days of meetings, 101 were spent discussing the constitutional text and 114 days went into consideration of the Draft.

o: Was dissolved and reconstituted under the Indian Independence Act
Continued only as a drafting body until 26 November 1949
Also functioned as the Dominion legislature while continuing constitution-making
Transferred its legislative functions to the Provisional Parliament
bank.e: It wore two hats — constitution-maker and Dominion legislature. The Provisional Parliament came into being only after 26 January 1950.

bank.q: Match List I (challenge before the Assembly) with List II (its constitutional response):
pairs: A. Fear of Balkanisation after Partition
1. Fundamental Rights combined with Directive Principles
4. Roles for Hindi, English and regional languages
bank.e: Balkanisation fear → strong-Centre federalism; liberty with reform → the FR–DPSP pairing; language → a three-tier compromise; communal violence → secular citizenship and minority safeguards.

bank.q: Which one of the following is NOT an accurate description of the Assembly's method?
o: Stage-wise constitution-making through preliminary, first, second and third readings
Clause-by-clause discussion of the Draft Constitution
Drafting confined strictly to Assembly members, with no external input
Committee-driven functioning with Steering, Credentials and House Committees
bank.e: Constitution-making was not sealed off. Archives record petitions and feedback from organisations, groups and individuals — an early instance of public participation in law-making.

bank.q: Who spoke the most in the Constituent Assembly debates, which ran to roughly 36 lakh words?
bank.e: Ambedkar, as Chairman of the Drafting Committee, spoke more than any other member — he had to defend nearly every clause against the 2,473 amendments moved.

bank.as: The Constitution has been criticised as a borrowed document.
bank.rs: The framers adapted borrowed institutions to Indian conditions rather than transplanting them.
bank.e: Both statements are true, but the Reason does not explain the Assertion — it rebuts it. The criticism arises from the fact of borrowing; the adaptation is the answer to that criticism, not its cause.
